author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: While digging in his San Francisco garden, a gardener stumbled upon an intriguing limestone sculpture. Despite consultations with around fifty experts, its origins remain shrouded in mystery. Given its location near an art school, there may be historical ties to the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition. The enigmatic bust is set to grace the garden as a captivating centerpiece.
title: SF man unearths 150-pound mystery limestone sculpture in backyard

author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
description: Frank Lloyd Wright’s only Tennessee home, the historic Shavin House in Chattanooga, has sold at auction for $4 million after remaining with the same family for 74 years. Completed in 1952, the 1,784-square-foot Usonian home was listed for $1.6 million. The property features crab orchard stone, Louisiana cypress, expansive windows and river views.
title: After 74 years with one family, Frank Lloyd Wright home sells for $4m
